newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp says EMU delay would cause mark to rise.
newsitem.headline: Krupp says EMU delay would cause mark to rise.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Tuesday that any delay in the start of European Economic and Monetary Union set for 1999 was likely to result in a sharp revaluation of the German mark.

Germany's economy unexpectedly turned lower late last year due in part to the strength of the German currency on the foreign exchange. "Any delay would bring a new revaluation wave," said Krupp, attending an event in Hamburg.
"Anyone who demands a delay in the start of the project is clearly not aware of the consequences," he added.

European nations hope to meld their currencies into a single currency from 1999, but have to meet certain ecoonoic targets to be admitted for entry. Many are facing problems reaching these goals, triggering talk of a possible delay.

Krupp said that the introduction of the European currency would create greater economic stability in Europe. He added that this was particularly important for German companies as they have a high export quota.
